questions.q: Explain in your own words how the description of the banyan tree's figs (tkequ) contributes to the story's atmosphere before the conflict begins.
questions.a: The figs symbolize nature's unconditional giving—they ripen and fall freely for anyone (birds, children, travelers) without discrimination. This creates an atmosphere of abundance, harmony, and organic community. A wrong answer focusing only on plot ("the figs attract people") misses the atmospheric function: the sensory detail of sweet, freely available fruit establishes a mood of natural justice that sharply contrasts with the later artificial scarcity imposed by bureaucracy.

questions.q: Create a brief descriptive paragraph (50-60 words) that establishes a setting and atmosphere for a modern-day equivalent of this conflict: a community space threatened by "development." Use sensory details and show, don't tell.
questions.a:
The metro pillar rises where the neem tree stood—its shade once measured in laughter, now in square meters of concrete. Dust coats the tea-stall's plastic chairs; the chai-wala wipes sweat with a GST invoice. Children's marbles roll into storm drains. A banner flaps: "Smart City. Green Future." No birds sing at noon.  
*Criteria met: sensory details (dust, sweat, sound), contrast (shade vs. concrete, marbles vs. drains), irony (banner), atmospheric tension.* A poor answer would state the conflict directly ("The government cut the tree for a metro") instead of evoking it through setting.
